sections.html: The tiger barb is still often known under the wrong name Barbus or Puntius tetrazona. The species correctly named Puntigrus tetrazona is never kept in aquaria or traded; the fish sold is exclusively the close relative Puntigrus anchisporus. The two species can easily be distinguished by the colour of the ventral fins, which are pitch-black in tetrazona and deep red in anchisporus.
Due to the extreme play instinct of this species, tiger barbs should never be kept with fish species that require quiet or that have extended fins.

The sport "moss green" of P. anchisporus was developed in the 1970s. In this sport the dark vertical stripes of the wild form are fused into one solid zone. In all other respects these moss greens are typical tiger barbs: swashbucklers that never show fear.
